title.narrative: AAS - Developing the Humanities and the Humanists of Asia
AAS - Developing the Humanities and the Humanists of Asia

description.narrative:
The Developing the Humanities and Social Sciences and Supporting Under-Represented Scholars of Asia has the following impact-level objectives:
- develop the research capacity of local universities and enhance the academic knowledge, research skills, experience and resources of their scholars in the humanities and social sciences, with a particular focus on junior faculty, graduate students, senior and independent scholars, women and ethnic minority groups.
- develop the research capabilities in post-conflict and conflict areas while helping to reduce the social and economic vulnerabilities of Southeast and South Asian low and lower-middle income countries through policy-relevant research.
- strengthen civil society and shape policies to help the selected countries and regions achieve their development goals.

The "Developing the Humanities and Social Sciences Supporting Under-represented Scholars of Asia" project aims to strengthen research capacity, and to produce new knowledge that will have positive development impacts in the sub-regions. Eligible beneficiaries of the project will be scholars, junior faculty members and post-graduate students from South and Southeast Asia. Members of ethnic minorities and marginalized groups, and academic institutions located in areas with high rates of poverty and risk for conflict will be especially prioritized. Knowledge production related to gender, human rights, democracy, conflict, environmental sustainability, and climate change will be supported.
The cooperation partner for this agreement is the Association for Asian Studies (AAS, Ann Arbor, USA). AAS is a non-profit organization with a mission to advance the field of Asian studies through international exchange, publications, networking, research and career development. The programme of support will be implemented by AAS in cooperation with the Regional Center for Social Science and Sustainable Development (RCSD, Chiang Mai, Thailand), the Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities at the Royal University of Phnom Penh (RUPP, Phnom Penh, Cambodia), the Faculty of Humanities at Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU, Pune, India), the School of Humanities and Social Sciences at Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS, Lahore, Pakistan), and The National University of Timor Leste (Dili, Timor Leste). The programme will be coordinated and governed by a Coordination and Collaboration Committee consisting of AAS and the five partner universities.
The programme has the following impact-level objectives:
- develop the research capacity of local universities and enhance the academic knowledge, research skills, experience and resources of their scholars in the humanities and social sciences, with a particular focus on junior faculty, graduate students, senior and independent scholars, women and ethnic minority groups.
- develop the research capabilities in post-conflict and conflict areas while helping to reduce the social and economic vulnerabilities of Southeast and South Asian low and lower-middle income countries through policy-relevant research.
- strengthen civil society and shape policies to help the selected countries and regions achieve their development goals.
The objectives will be reached through a range of activities that include individual research scholarships and fellowships, capacity building workshops and trainings, publication support, and networking and communication support.
In the medium to long-term, it is expected that the capacity built during this phase of activities will contribute to stronger academic institutions in poor and post-conflict areas of South and Southeast Asia.

"Developing the Humanities and Social Sciences Supporting Under-represented Scholars of Asia" syftar till att stärka forskningskapacitet och kunskapsproduktion med relevans för hållbar, inklusive och jämställd utveckling i regionen. Projektet kommer att stödja forskare, doktorander och mastersstudenter i Syd- och Sydostasien. Projektet prioriterar medlemmar av etniska minoriteter och marginaliserade grupper, samt forskare som tillhör akademiska institutioner belägna i områden med hög fattigdom och/eller risk för konflikt. Kunskapsproduktion har fokus på tema av relevans för Sveriges regionala biståndsstrategi inklusive genus, mänskliga rättigheter, demokrati, konflikt, miljömässig hållbarhet och klimatförändringar.
Sidas avtalspartner är Association for Asian Studies (AAS, Ann Arbor, USA). AAS är en ideell organisation med ett uppdrag att främja Asienstudier genom internationellt utbyte, publikationer, nätverk, forskning och karriärutveckling. Programmet kommer att genomföras av AAS i samarbete med Regional Centre for Social Science and Sustainable Development (RCSD, Chiang Mai, Thailand), Fakulteten för samhällsvetenskap och humaniora vid Royal University of Phnom Penh (RUPP, Phnom Penh, Kambodja), Fakulteten för humaniora vid Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU, Pune, Indien), School of Humanities and Social Sciences vid Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS, Lahore, Pakistan) och National University of Timor Leste (Dili, Östtimor). Programmet kommer att samordnas och styras av en kommitté (CCC) bestående av representanter från AAS och de fem partneruniversitet.
Programmet har följande mål:
- bidra till stärkt forskningskapacitet hos forskare och forskningsinstitutioner inom humaniora och samhällsvetenskap, med särskilt fokus på juniora lärare, doktorander, kvinnor och medlemmar av etnisk minoritet grupper.
- utveckla forskningskapacitet i post-konflikt- och konfliktområden och samtidigt bidra till minskade sociala och ekonomiska sårbarheterna i låginkomstländer i sydöstra och södra Asien genom relevant kunskapsproduktion.
- starka samarbetet mellan forskare och det civila samhället, samt bidra till evidens-baserade policyer som främjar hållbart utveckling.
Målen kommer att nås genom en rad aktiviteter som inkluderar individuella forskningsstipendier, kapacitetsbyggande workshops och utbildningar, publiceringsstöd och nätverks- och forskningskommunikationsstöd.
På längre sikt kommer satsningen på forskare bidra till stärkande av forskningsinstitutioner och universitet inom fattiga och postkonfliktområden i Syd- och Sydostasien.

During 2024, AAS together with university partners achieved several key results:
i) A greater number of fellows selected from underrepresented regions across South and Southeast Asia
During 2024, 25 CHSS scholars of the second cohort had been selected from the 2023 research grant selection process from 1843 applicants. These 25 CHSS research grantees come from Philippines, Cambodia, Lao PDR, Thailand, Vietnam, Timor Leste, India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka. Their research projects deal with issues from documentary making on Cambodian migrants to linguistic study and preservation in the central hills of Laos or forest preservation and conservation in the Philippines, to media coverage and public discourse around enforced disappearances in Bangladesh.
ii) More CHSS workshops were decentralized in remote and economically vulnerable areas as results of university hubs gaining more capacity and experiences benefited from the CHSS project and interactions with AAS and CHSSs other university hubs
During 2024, implementing partners in Cambodia, Thailand, Timor Leste, India and Pakistan organized a total of 13 in person workshops and 2 virtual workshops. For instance, the university hub in Thailand organized one of their workshops in Vientiane, Laos, to attract participants from Lao PDR, as well as from other low and lower income countries (i.e. Myanmar). The university hub in India worked with two of their fellows to co-organized two writing workshops in collaboration with local institutions in the economically vulnerable states of Jharkhand and Assam. Two writing workshops were also held virtually with Timorese scholars to help them publish their articles. As a result, CHSS university hubs were able to enhance the visibility of the CHSS project to attract early career scholars from less well equipped institutions to participate in AAS training, symposia and conferences in Asia and the US, thereby helped enhance their exposures to international academic excellences.
iii) More fellows successfully applying for international conferences and postdoctoral fellowships being engaged with the CHSS project as scholars and research grantees ' Thanks to Sweden's scholarships, more than 40 CHSS research grantees, including a postdoc researcher, and 20 workshop participants from all university hubs in India, Pakistan, Cambodia, Thailand and Timor Leste could participate and present their research projects in the AAS 2024 Mobility Beyond Boundaries Symposium in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Their research focused on the important theme of mobilities beyond margins from the geographical through to the social and professional lenses presented in seven panels on Scarred Cartographies of the Colonial Legacy, Strategies of Mobility during Occupation and Hardship, Conflicts, Refugees and Landlessness, Climate Mutability and Forced Displacements, Human Rights to Mobility and Immobility, Genders Fluidity and Womens Movements and Higher Education as a Site of Upward Social and Spatial Mobility.
The 2024 Symposium and other two workshops were organized in connection to the 2024 AAS-in-Asia Annual Conference with 1485 participants, 344 scheduled sessions and 22 special events with 175200 proposals. Within this AAS Conference, the CHSS had 19 panels and roundtables scheduled in the program and 64 CHSS fellow participants from 9 countries.
iv) CHSS scholars have gained personal career advancements
A number of 9 publications from Pakistan, 5 from India, 2 from Timor Leste and 2 from Cambodia were made. Their publications featured stories in films and books and journals on local traditional music, climate change and ethnic community survival strategies in Pakistan, forced repatriation of Cambodian refugees, pastureland conservation and ecotourism in Bhutan, as well as LGBTQ rights in Timor Leste, local identities in India and Kashmir. Many of these projects directly support sustainable development, particularly in education and digital transformation. Eleven researchers from Pakistan have contributed to public engagement through popular science publications, newspaper articles, and public talks, making research more accessible to a wider audience.
vi) CHSS members received complementary funding from Asia and US based partners
Under 2024, the CHSS received $35,000 from the Forest Foundation Philippines (FFP) as direct support of five CHSS fellows of Filipinos nationals. These fellows have successfully completed their ethnographic research on climate change, local adaptation and the preservation of indigenous cultures. As part of a larger grant, the Henry Luce Foundation has contributed $53,280 to support underrepresented scholars of Asia. Developing South and Southeast Asian Connectivities across the Asian Studies Network was specifically designed to bring underserved Asianists to AAS-CHSS annual meetings in North America (Seattle in 2024 and Columbus in 2025). Additional sponsorship amounting to $7,000 was also provided by the Luce Foundation to facilitate the participation of CHSS fellows in the 2024 AAS-in-Asia in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, by covering their registration fees.
